subChunks.title: Performance and the JIT Scanner
subChunks.hookHtml: Tailwind's scanner is the reason production CSS stays tiny. It only emits the classes you actually use. But it learns what you use by scanning source files as plain text — not by executing your code. Understanding this distinction prevents the most common production bug in every Tailwind codebase.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Master Ember: "Tailwind's great virtue is that it emits nothing you do not use. Its great trap is that it decides what you use by reading your source files as text — not executing them. Tailwind v4 removed the content array. The scanning rule itself did not change."

How the scanner works in v4

Tailwind v4 automatically detects your project files — no content array required. It reads all relevant source files, looks for strings that match utility patterns, and emits only those utilities via text matching — no JavaScript execution.

/* For edge cases, tell the scanner where to look: */
@import "tailwindcss";

/* ✅ Include a component library in node_modules */
@source "../node_modules/@my-org/ui/src/**/*.tsx";

/* ❌ Never include your own compiled CSS — circular scan */

The dynamic class trap — the #1 production bug

Always manifests the same way: works in development, wrong in production.

// ❌ BROKEN — 'text-red-500' never appears as a complete string
const statusClass = `text-${status === 'error' ? 'red' : 'green'}-500`;

// In dev: may still render (HMR keeps a broader set)
// In production: scanner never found these classes. No CSS emitted.

// ✅ CORRECT — complete strings visible in source
const statusClasses = {
  error:   'text-red-500',
  success: 'text-green-500',
  warning: 'text-yellow-500',
};
<p className={statusClasses[status] ?? 'text-gray-500'}>

The rule is absolute: never construct a Tailwind class by interpolating a fragment of it. The full class string must appear verbatim in a scanned file.

Safelisting — for classes from external data

/* Safelist exact classes */
@source inline("text-red-500 text-green-500 bg-red-100 bg-green-100");

/* Pattern syntax — generates a family of classes */
@source inline("{bg,text}-{red,green,blue}-{100,500,900}");

Checking your bundle size

After npm run build, inspect dist/assets/*.css. A well-built Tailwind app is typically 8–25 KB gzipped. Red flags:

  • 100+ KB: an @source path is matching node_modules broadly or a large JSON data file
  • Styles missing in prod: dynamic class interpolation bug

Arbitrary values — when they are and aren't appropriate

// ✅ One-off pixel-perfect value from design spec
<div class="top-[57px]">  // navbar is exactly 57px

// ❌ Value used in 15 places — belongs in @theme
<div class="mt-[17px]">   // add --spacing-4.25: 17px to @theme

// ✅ CSS expressions not available as a token
<div class="w-[calc(100%-4rem)]">

Ember: "Arbitrary values are an escape hatch, not a shortcut. When they accumulate, the @theme config is failing to represent the design system."

storyBeats.text: Master Ember places a thin book titled 'The Scanner' on the workbench. He does not open it.

storyBeats.speaker: Master Ember
storyBeats.text: The scanner reads your source files as text. It does not execute your JavaScript. If a complete class string does not appear verbatim in a scanned file, that class does not exist in production.

storyBeats.speaker: Safe dynamic class map — the fix is always the same

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a status badge system the safe way — all class strings complete and static:

  • .status-active: bg-green-100, text-green-800, border, border-green-200, text-xs, font-semibold, px-2.5, py-0.5, rounded-full
  • .status-inactive: bg-gray-100, text-gray-700, border, border-gray-200, text-xs, font-semibold, px-2.5, py-0.5, rounded-full
  • .status-error: bg-red-100, text-red-800, border, border-red-200, text-xs, font-semibold, px-2.5, py-0.5, rounded-full
  • .status-warning: bg-yellow-100, text-yellow-800, border, border-yellow-200, text-xs, font-semibold, px-2.5, py-0.5, rounded-full

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Write three versions of a status chip — success, warning, error — from scratch. Version 1: a safe approach with full class strings per variant. Version 2: the broken dynamic approach. Version 3: the fixed safelist/lookup-object approach. Structure them as three separate HTML elements with comments explaining each.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain to someone who only knows HTML/CSS why `text-${color}-500` works in development but breaks in production. Use the word 'scanner' in your explanation.

questions.prompt: How does Tailwind v4 determine which utility classes to include in the production build?
options: It automatically scans project source files as plain text, including only classes found as complete strings
It executes your JavaScript code and tracks which classes are applied at runtime
It imports all possible utilities and tree-shakes unused ones at bundle time
It reads your CSS file and generates utilities for every selector found
questions.answer: It automatically scans project source files as plain text, including only classes found as complete strings
questions.explanation: Tailwind is a text scanner, not a JS evaluator. In v4, files are detected automatically — no content array needed. Complete class strings must be present verbatim in a scanned file. Interpolated fragments like `text-${color}-500` produce no complete class string and are not emitted.

questions.prompt: In Tailwind v4, how do you safelist class names that come from a CMS or API and cannot appear verbatim in source?
options: @source inline("bg-red-500 text-red-500 bg-green-500") in your CSS file
Add the classes to a safelist.txt file in the project root
Dynamic classes are automatically included — no safelisting needed in v4
questions.answer: @source inline("bg-red-500 text-red-500 bg-green-500") in your CSS file
questions.explanation: In v4, safelisting uses the @source inline() directive in your CSS file. You can list exact class names or use brace expansion patterns: @source inline("{bg,text}-{red,green}-{100,500}"). This replaces the safelist array in tailwind.config.js from v3.

questions.prompt: A developer writes className={`bg-${post.category}-100 text-${post.category}-800`} for category badges. It works in development but shows no background colour in production. What happened?
options: The scanner saw only fragments ('bg-' and '-100'), never a complete class string — those utilities were not emitted in production
The JIT compiler disabled background utilities in production mode for performance
The CSS variables for category colours were not defined in @theme
Tailwind v4 no longer supports template literal class names — they must be migrated to @apply
questions.answer: The scanner saw only fragments ('bg-' and '-100'), never a complete class string — those utilities were not emitted in production
questions.explanation: Dev mode has a broader initial compilation, masking the bug. The production scanner is strict — only emit what was found as a complete string. Fix 1: a lookup object mapping each category to its complete class strings. Fix 2: @source inline("{bg,text}-{news,sport,tech}-{100,800}") in the CSS file.
